content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon when true values are rising sharply — model lags behind actual momentum.
- Shows strong bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., 70+), underestimating upward trends.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 68+ → 69+), then corrects too late — model overreacts and overcorrects.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to prior levels too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to be too conservative in the first 10 days, then gradually overcorrect as true values rise.
- Model fails to capture “late-stage breakout” momentum — often misses final 5–7 days of price acceleration.
